item.content:encoded:
Seconding this. Ratings, especially in regards to tales and GoI formats, simply aren’t a very good attribute to an article’s merit.

Most tales don’t get nearly the same clicks as most SCP articles, so IMO a “good tale rating” is on average closer to +40. Honestly, it just seems a bit like snubbing people who write non-scp articles by accident because tales can typically languish at +15 despite having quality ideas.

That’s just my take, though. Not trying to seem salty or anything. I love the art here!

item.content:encoded:
Votes don't help the author, so I've vowed to always leave a comment with mine, at the very least whenever I rate an article negatively. If you feel the same, help out by leaving critique with more of your votes. Comment follows:

As a set of achievements, I do not get a good vibe from these. I explain my thoughts in more detail on the other achievements page. Primarily I don't like how the achievements reward ratings, which are not a good measure of a page's quality or of an author's worth.

It makes far more sense to me to reward good, ongoing contributions to the site, like pages authored in a canon.

A lot of the achievements on this page specifically are just not good at all. "Holding the highest number of reviewers-spotlight articles in the site." can only be achieved by one person. "Author of at least 10 [pages that] are downvoted by the same member." encourages malicious downvoting. A lot of the achievements simply encourage repetition of tropes and clichés. There's also this weird mix of incredibly specific achievements and incredibly generic ones.

As an artwork page, the icons are actually pretty good. So it's a novote from me overall.
